content: 1. The GRADE Evidence to Decision (EtD) frameworks provide a systematic and transparent methodology for making well-informed healthcare decisions. 2. Alonso et al. conducted a study revealing a global treatment gap for anxiety disorders, based on data from the World Mental Health Surveys across 21 countries. 3. Porritt, Gomersall, and Lockwood described the processes of study selection and critical appraisal in systematic reviews conducted by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI). 4. Lewin et al. introduced the application of GRADE-CERQual to qualitative evidence synthesis findings, emphasizing its role in improving the reliability of qualitative research. 5. Lewin and colleagues further explored the use of qualitative evidence synthesis (QES) findings to inform evidence-to-decision frameworks and guideline recommendations. 6. The second edition of the Atlas: Country Resources for Neurological Disorders provides a comprehensive overview of global resources for neurological conditions. 7. The Mental Health Atlas 2020 offers updated insights into mental health resources and services worldwide. 8. Agabio et al. reviewed the efficacy of baclofen in treating alcohol use disorder, as documented in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 9. The ICD-10 classification system outlines diagnostic criteria for mental and behavioral disorders, serving as a critical tool for research and clinical practice. 10. The DSM-IV, published by the American Psychiatric Association, provides diagnostic criteria for mental disorders and has been a cornerstone in psychiatric practice since 1994. 11. The ICD-11, the latest revision of the International Classification of Diseases, is accessible online and reflects advancements in disease classification. 12. The DSM-5, the fifth edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, represents a significant update in the classification of mental health conditions. 13. Sundström et al. reviewed computer-based interventions for problematic alcohol use, summarizing findings from systematic reviews. 14. The WHO guideline on digital interventions for health system strengthening provides evidence-based recommendations for leveraging technology in healthcare. 15. Agabio et al. examined the combined use of pharmacological and psychosocial interventions for alcohol use disorder in a Cochrane review. 16. Chawla et al. conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis of drug treatments for panic disorder, with or without agoraphobia, based on randomized controlled trials. 17. Slee et al. reviewed pharmacological treatments for generalized anxiety disorder, presenting a network meta-analysis of available evidence. 18. Parker et al. analyzed contemporary treatments for anxiety in primary care settings, focusing on outcomes in countries with universal healthcare. 19. Haller et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of acceptanceand mindfulness-based interventions for DSM-5 anxiety disorders. 20. Van Dis et al. reviewed the long-term outcomes of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for anxiety-related disorders, highlighting its sustained efficacy. 21. Papola et al. evaluated psychological and social interventions for preventing mental disorders in lowand middle-income countries affected by humanitarian crises. 22. Barkowski et al. assessed the efficacy of group psychotherapy for anxiety disorders through a systematic review and meta-analysis. 23. Pauley et al. reviewed two decades of digital interventions for anxiety disorders, analyzing their treatment effectiveness. 24. Kim and Kim examined the effects of relaxation therapy on anxiety disorders, presenting findings from a systematic review and meta-analysis. 25. Ramos-Sanchez et al. updated the meta-analytic evidence on the anxiolytic effects of exercise for individuals with anxiety and related disorders. 26. Vancampfort et al. analyzed dropout rates from exercise-based randomized controlled trials among individuals with anxiety and stress-related disorders. 27. Machado et al. explored whether regular physical exercise could serve as a treatment for panic disorder, based on a systematic review. 28. The WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behavior provide evidence-based recommendations for promoting health through movement. 29. Breilmann et al. compared the efficacy of benzodiazepines versus placebo for treating panic disorder in adults, as documented in a Cochrane review. 30. Shinfuku et al. reviewed the long-term effectiveness and safety of benzodiazepine use in anxiety disorders, presenting a meta-analysis of available data. 31. Xiao et al. conducted a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to evaluate the effectiveness of enhanced evidence-based care for depressive disorders. 32. Stein et al. reviewed the impact of psychiatric and psychosomatic consultation-liaison services in general hospitals on symptoms of depression and anxiety. 33. Van der Feltz-Cornelis et al. examined treatments for comorbid depressive disorder or subthreshold depression in individuals with diabetes mellitus. 34. Cortese et al. compared the efficacy and tolerability of medications for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children, adolescents, and adults. 35. Pandey et al. reviewed the effectiveness of universal self-regulation-based interventions in children and adolescents, focusing on outcomes from a meta-analysis. 36. Caldwell et al. evaluated school-based interventions aimed at preventing anxiety, depression, and conduct disorders in children and young people. 37. Smith et al. conducted a meta-analytic review of randomized controlled trials on the Good Behavior Game, assessing its impact on behavior modification. 38. Lannes et al. reviewed preventive interventions for children of parents with mental illness, presenting findings from a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. 39. Wang et al. systematically reviewed the use of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for autism spectrum disorders, focusing on its efficacy. 40. Soares et al. analyzed the effectiveness of social skills training for autism spectrum disorder, comparing in-person and technological interventions. 41. Wolstencroft et al. reviewed group social skills interventions for children with high-functioning autism spectrum disorder, presenting a meta-analysis of outcomes. 42. Sharma et al. reviewed the use of cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety in children and young people on the autism spectrum, presenting a meta-analysis. 43. Storebø et al. evaluated social skills training for ADHD in children aged 5 to 18 years, based on a Cochrane review. 44. Cortese et al. conducted a meta-analysis of cognitive training interventions for ADHD, focusing on clinical and neuropsychological outcomes. 45. Bikic et al. reviewed organizational skills interventions for children and adolescents with ADHD, presenting findings from a meta-analysis. 46. Reichow et al. reviewed beginning reading interventions for children and adolescents with intellectual disabilities, based on a Cochrane review. 47. Rinaldi et al. systematically reviewed the efficacy of treatments for developmental language disorder, presenting findings from a meta-analysis. 48. Brignell et al. reviewed interventions for children and adolescents who stutter, presenting a systematic review, meta-analysis, and evidence map. 49. Ahn and Hwang conducted a meta-analysis of cognitive rehabilitation interventions for adaptive behavior in children with neurodevelopmental disorders. 50. Huang et al. reviewed the effects of physical activity interventions on children and adolescents with autism, presenting findings from a meta-analysis. 51. Sun et al. analyzed the effects of physical exercise on attention deficit and other major symptoms in children with ADHD, based on a meta-analysis. 52. Cerrillo-Urbiná et al. reviewed the effects of physical exercise in children with ADHD, presenting findings from randomized controlled trials. 53. Ciullo et al. conducted a meta-analysis of intervention research for students with learning disabilities in social studies. 54. Jitendra et al. reviewed mathematical interventions for secondary students with learning disabilities and mathematics difficulties, presenting a meta-analysis. 55. Miyahara et al. reviewed task-oriented interventions for children with developmental coordination disorder, based on a Cochrane review. 56. Liang et al. evaluated the effectiveness of exercise interventions for children with cerebral palsy, presenting findings from a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. 57. Dobson et al. reviewed the efficacy and tolerability of pharmacotherapy for pediatric anxiety disorders, presenting findings from a network meta-analysis. 58. Hetrick et al. reviewed new-generation antidepressants for depression in children and adolescents, presenting findings from a network meta-analysis. 59. Zhou et al. compared the efficacy and acceptability of antidepressants, psychotherapies, and their combination for treating depressive disorders in children and adolescents. 60. Li et al. reviewed the risk of suicidal behaviors associated with antidepressant exposure in children and adolescents, presenting findings from a meta-analysis of observational studies. 61. The National Collaborating Centre for Mental Health (UK) provided guidelines for managing post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in adults and children in primary and secondary care. 62. Bisson and Andrew reviewed psychological treatments for PTSD, presenting findings from a Cochrane review. 63. Cohen et al. provided an empirical update on trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy for children and adolescents. 64. Phelps et al. updated the Australian guidelines for the prevention and treatment of PTSD, reflecting advancements in the third edition. 65. Cheng et al. reviewed the effectiveness of nonpharmacological interventions for informal dementia caregivers, presenting findings from a meta-analysis. 66. González-Fraile et al. reviewed remotely delivered information, training, and support for informal caregivers of people with dementia, based on a Cochrane review. 67. Lee et al. reviewed effective interventions for depressive symptoms among caregivers, presenting findings from a systematic review.
